comp_chem/aqsol/alignment/base.csv.description: AqSolDB solubility subset for train-test alignment experiments -- the full AqSolDB set with no train-test structural overlap constraint. The four alignment subsets share a schema and differ only in how structurally similar their compounds are to the training pool, which isolates how much a reported metric depends on that similarity.

columns.name: Compound name
columns.solubility: log10 of aqueous solubility in mol/L (prediction target)
columns.sd: Standard deviation across the contributing source measurements
columns.ocurrences: Number of sources reporting this compound

references: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-019-0151-1 (Sorkun et al., AqSolDB, Sci Data 2019)

comp_chem/logd/logd_all.csv.description: Merged and deduplicated experimental LogD (octanol-water distribution coefficient at pH 7.4) dataset. Standardized using the ChEMBL pipeline so SMILES are joinable to logp_all.csv. Currently a single source; structured for additional sources to be merged in.

columns.smiles: Standardized canonical SMILES (RDKit, neutralized, canonical tautomer)
columns.logd: Mean experimental logD at pH 7.4 across sources
columns.logd_std: Standard deviation of logD across sources (0 if single source)
columns.logd_count: Number of sources reporting this compound
columns.logd_values: Pipe-delimited individual logD values from each source

references: https://moleculenet.org/datasets-1 (AstraZeneca logD via ChEMBL, MoleculeNet mirror)

comp_chem/logd/logd_astrazeneca_chembl.c.description: AstraZeneca experimental logD measurements at pH 7.4 (~4,200 compounds), originally published in ChEMBL. Fetched directly from the MoleculeNet S3 mirror; same data is also redistributed by DeepChem and Therapeutic Data Commons (as `Lipophilicity_AstraZeneca`).

columns.smiles: Standardized structure (salt-stripped, neutralized, canonical tautomer) -- use this for modeling and joining
columns.smiles_orig: Structure exactly as provided by the source, before standardization
columns.logd: Experimental logD at pH 7.4 (octanol-water distribution coefficient)

comp_chem/logp/logp_all.csv.description: Merged and deduplicated experimental LogP (octanol-water partition coefficient) dataset from multiple public sources. Standardized using the ChEMBL pipeline (salt removal, charge neutralization, tautomer canonicalization). Multi-component mixtures dropped; known pharmaceutical counterions stripped. For compounds present in SangsterLogP (Cirino et al. 2026 — the most rigorously curated source), the `logp` value is taken from SangsterLogP; otherwise it is the cross-source mean (see `primary_source` column). Joinable on `smiles` to logd_all.csv.

columns.smiles: Standardized canonical SMILES (RDKit, neutralized, canonical tautomer)
columns.logp: Experimental logP — Sangster value if present, else cross-source mean
columns.logp_std: Standard deviation of logP across all reporting sources (0 if single source)
columns.logp_count: Number of sources reporting this compound
columns.sources: Pipe-delimited list of source names that reported this compound
columns.primary_source: Which source the `logp` value was taken from: 'sangster' or 'consensus' (mean across non-Sangster sources)
columns.logp_values: Pipe-delimited individual logP values from each source

comp_chem/logp/logp_graphormer_logp.csv.description: GraphormerLogP (GLP) experimental LogP dataset (~42,000 compounds). Multi-source curation by the Chemoinformatics and Molecular Modeling Laboratory (CIMM) at Kazan Federal University. Aggregated from OpenChem, Huuskonen, SAMPL6/7, and other published datasets.

columns.smiles: Standardized structure (salt-stripped, neutralized, canonical tautomer) -- use this for modeling and joining
columns.smiles_orig: Structure exactly as provided by the source, before standardization

references: https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jcim.4c00654 (Safin et al., GraphormerLogP, J Chem Inf Model 2024)

comp_chem/logp/logp_opera_physprop.csv.description: PHYSPROP/OPERA experimental LogP training data (~4,200 compounds). Curated by the EPA from the PHYSPROP database, originally used to train the KOWWIN and OPERA LogP models. Extracted from OPERA_Data.zip in the NIEHS/OPERA GitHub repository.

columns.smiles: Standardized structure (salt-stripped, neutralized, canonical tautomer) -- use this for modeling and joining
columns.smiles_orig: Structure exactly as provided by the source, before standardization

references: https://doi.org/10.1186/s13321-018-0263-1 (Mansouri et al., OPERA models, J Cheminform 2018)

comp_chem/logp/logp_sangster.csv.description: SangsterLogP experimental LogP dataset (~23,500 compounds), the largest publicly curated logP collection. Originates from Dr. James Sangster's review of >3,000 published sources, curated via the OCHEM platform with systematic logD-to-logP correction for ionisable compounds (ChemAxon pKa + ΔDP shift) and consensus-based outlier/duplicate removal. Spans -3.8 to 11.7 log units and includes ~800 beyond-Rule-of-5 (MW > 700) compounds, substantially expanding chemical space coverage vs PHYSPROP. Distributed under CC-BY-4.0 via Zenodo. The `logp` column here is the experimental-or-adjusted value (logD measurements corrected to logP via ΔDP) from the main sheet of the source XLSX.

columns.smiles: Standardized structure (salt-stripped, neutralized, canonical tautomer) -- use this for modeling and joining
columns.smiles_orig: Structure exactly as provided by the source, before standardization
columns.logp: Experimental or adjusted logP (octanol-water partition coefficient)

references: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-026-07357-2 (Cirino, Caron, Ermondi, Charochkina, Tetko; SangsterLogP: the largest publicly available dataset of logP values, Sci Data 2026)
Sangster, J. Octanol-Water Partition Coefficients of Simple Organic Compounds. J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 18, 1111-1229 (1989). https://doi.org/10.1063/1.555833

comp_chem/logp_logd/overlap_00_03.csv.description: Multi-task LogD/LogP dataset, LOW-overlap tier. All 4,199 LogD compounds plus LogP rows whose best-Tanimoto-to-LogD falls in [0.0, 0.3) — auxiliary chemistry the LogD set doesn't cover. Tests whether 'novel' auxiliary representation transfers to LogD prediction. Auxiliary LogP rows share no SMILES with LogD. Built by data/public_data/build_logp_logd_overlap.py.

columns.smiles: Standardized canonical SMILES (joinable to logp_all.csv and logd_all.csv)
columns.logd: Experimental logD at pH 7.4 (NaN if not measured)

comp_chem/logp_logd/overlap_03_07.csv.description: Multi-task LogD/LogP dataset, MEDIUM-overlap tier. All 4,199 LogD compounds plus LogP rows whose best-Tanimoto-to-LogD falls in [0.3, 0.7). The band excludes Tanimoto = 1.0, so the auxiliary LogP rows share no SMILES with LogD — no rows have both columns populated. Auxiliary chemistry is similar to LogD's neighborhood without duplicating it; this tier represents the 'complementary supervision' mode. Built by data/public_data/build_logp_logd_overlap.py.

columns.smiles: Standardized canonical SMILES (joinable to logp_all.csv and logd_all.csv)
columns.logd: Experimental logD at pH 7.4 (NaN if not measured)

comp_chem/logp_logd/overlap_07_10.csv.description: Multi-task LogD/LogP dataset, HIGH-overlap tier. All 4,199 LogD compounds plus LogP rows whose best-Tanimoto-to-LogD falls in [0.7, 1.0]. The band includes Tanimoto = 1.0 (exact-SMILES matches), so a portion of rows have both `logp` and `logd` populated — these are the same compounds measured in both source datasets. Auxiliary chemistry is close to LogD's; this tier represents the 'duplicate / nearby supervision' mode. Built by data/public_data/build_logp_logd_overlap.py.

columns.smiles: Standardized canonical SMILES (joinable to logp_all.csv and logd_all.csv)
columns.logd: Experimental logD at pH 7.4 (NaN if not measured)

comp_chem/openadmet/octant_cyp/inhibitio.description: CYP3A4 inhibition dose-response from the OpenADMET / Octant reactivity release. CYP3A4 metabolises roughly half of marketed drugs, so inhibition is a primary drug-drug-interaction liability. Published as a single set with no train-test split; the QC columns let you filter to well-behaved curves before training.

columns.id: Octant batch identifier for the assayed material
columns.cyp3a4_pic50: -log10(IC50 in M) for CYP3A4 inhibition (prediction target)
columns.cyp3a4_pic50_ci_lower: Lower bound of the 95% CI for cyp3a4_pic50
columns.cyp3a4_pic50_ci_upper: Upper bound of the 95% CI for cyp3a4_pic50
columns.slope_log2: Hill slope of the dose-response fit (log2)
columns.emax_log2fc: Maximal effect as a log2 fold change from control
columns.activity_status: Whether the compound registered as active
columns.rollover_status: Flag for non-monotonic 'rollover' at high concentration
columns.saturation_status: Whether the response saturated within the tested range
columns.direction: Direction of the effect (inhibition vs activation)
columns.qc_flag_primary: Primary QC flag for the measurement
columns.plate_qc_status: QC verdict for the assay plate

comp_chem/openadmet/octant_cyp/mass_spec.description: Mass-spectrometry ionization response for the Octant compound library ('will it fly in mass spec') -- peak areas under two mobile-phase additives. Predicts whether a compound is detectable by LC-MS at all, which gates every downstream MS-readout assay. Much larger than the assay files and mostly disjoint from them.

columns.id: Octant batch identifier for the assayed material
columns.ammonium_fluoride_area: Integrated peak area under ammonium fluoride mobile phase
columns.ammonium_formate_area: Integrated peak area under ammonium formate mobile phase

comp_chem/openadmet/octant_cyp/reactivit.description: Enzyme reactivity (substrate turnover) for CYP3A4 and CYP2J2 from the OpenADMET / Octant release. Long format: one row per compound-enzyme pair. Structures are joined in from inhibition.csv, which covers every batch present here.

columns.id: Octant batch identifier for the assayed material
columns.smiles: Standardized compound structure (SMILES), joined from inhibition.csv
columns.control: Raw signal in the no-enzyme control
columns.log10fc: log10 fold change, treatment vs control
columns.log2fc: log2 fold change, treatment vs control
columns.pct_remaining: Percent of compound remaining after treatment (prediction target)

comp_chem/openadmet/pxr/testing/blinded..description: Blinded activity-track test set (513 compounds) for the PXR challenge — SMILES only, ground-truth pEC50 withheld for scoring (Relative Absolute Error). Split into two analog sets: Analog Set 1 (scored on the Phase 1 live leaderboard, then unblinded on 2026-05-26 — see pxr_test_phase1_unblinded) and Analog Set 2 (held out for final scoring after 2026-07-01).

comp_chem/openadmet/pxr/testing/phase1_u.description: Analog Set 1 of the activity-track test set with ground-truth pEC50 revealed at the Phase 1 to Phase 2 transition (2026-05-26). Serves as a held-out evaluation set and as additional training signal for Phase 2 submissions targeting Analog Set 2.

columns.ocnt_batch: Octant batch identifier for the assayed material
columns.pec50_ci_lower: Lower bound of the 95% CI for pec50
columns.pec50_ci_upper: Upper bound of the 95% CI for pec50
columns.emax_estimate: Maximal induction efficacy (Emax) from the dose-response fit
columns.emax_ci_lower: Lower bound of the 95% CI for emax_estimate
columns.emax_ci_upper: Upper bound of the 95% CI for emax_estimate
columns.emax_vs_pos_ctrl_estimate: Emax expressed relative to the positive-control agonist
columns.emax_vs_pos_ctrl_ci_lower: Lower bound of the 95% CI for emax_vs_pos_ctrl_estimate
columns.emax_vs_pos_ctrl_ci_upper: Upper bound of the 95% CI for emax_vs_pos_ctrl_estimate
columns.phase: Challenge phase the compound belongs to

comp_chem/openadmet/pxr/testing/structur.description: Structure-track blinded test set: fragment-sized molecules for predicting protein-ligand complexes against PXR, scored by LDDT-PLI. Crystallographic data generated with the Fraser lab at UCSF. Distinct from the activity track.

comp_chem/openadmet/pxr/training/counter.description: PXR-null counter-assay training data. Reports the null-line (non-PXR / off-target) response used to flag and discount assay artifacts, so apparent PXR activity can be separated from non-specific signal.

columns.ocnt_batch: Octant batch identifier for the assayed material
columns.emax_vs_pos_ctrl_estimate: Counter-assay Emax relative to the positive-control agonist
columns.pec50_ci_lower: Lower bound of the 95% CI for pec50
columns.pec50_ci_upper: Upper bound of the 95% CI for pec50
columns.emax_ci_lower: Lower bound of the 95% CI for emax_estimate
columns.emax_ci_upper: Upper bound of the 95% CI for emax_estimate
columns.emax_vs_pos_ctrl_ci_lower: Lower bound of the 95% CI for emax_vs_pos_ctrl_estimate
columns.emax_vs_pos_ctrl_ci_upper: Upper bound of the 95% CI for emax_vs_pos_ctrl_estimate

comp_chem/openadmet/pxr/training/htchem_.description: High-throughput chemistry (HT-chem) library screening data, released during Phase 2 — library-scale measurements that broaden training coverage of chemical space. Measured on crude library material, with Charged Aerosol Detector (CAD) analytical columns used to correct potency by the actual measured compound concentration.

columns.crude_batch_id: Batch identifier for the crude library material
columns.crude_ec50s: EC50(s) measured on the crude material (M)
columns.crude_pec50s: pEC50(s) measured on the crude material
columns.crude_emax_normalized: Emax normalized to the positive control
columns.corrected_crude_ec50: EC50 corrected for measured compound concentration (M)
columns.cad_yield_volatility_note: Note on CAD yield / volatility caveats for this compound
columns.crude_theoretical_mass_on_column: Theoretical mass loaded on the LC column
columns.crude_actual_mass_on_column: Actual mass on column from CAD quantitation
columns.crude_correction_factor: Concentration correction factor applied to potency
columns.crude_cad_peak_area_cv: Coefficient of variation of the CAD peak area
columns.crude_cad_slope_cv: Coefficient of variation of the CAD calibration slope
columns.crude_cad_yield_se: Standard error of the CAD-derived yield

comp_chem/openadmet/pxr/training/main.cs.description: Primary training set for the OpenADMET PXR Induction Blind Challenge (activity track). Dose-response pEC50 and Emax for human Pregnane-X Receptor (hPXR) induction, measured with OpenADMET's in-house high-fidelity cell-based assay. PXR is the master regulator of CYP3A4 (which metabolises ~50% of marketed drugs), so PXR induction is a primary driver of drug-drug interaction liability.

columns.ocnt_batch: Octant batch identifier for the assayed material
columns.pec50: Dose-response potency, -log10(EC50 in M) — the challenge prediction target
columns.emax_estimate: Maximal induction efficacy (Emax) from the dose-response fit
columns.emax_vs_pos_ctrl_estimate: Emax expressed relative to the positive-control agonist
columns.pec50_ci_lower: Lower bound of the 95% CI for pec50
columns.pec50_ci_upper: Upper bound of the 95% CI for pec50
columns.emax_ci_lower: Lower bound of the 95% CI for emax_estimate
columns.emax_ci_upper: Upper bound of the 95% CI for emax_estimate
columns.emax_vs_pos_ctrl_ci_lower: Lower bound of the 95% CI for emax_vs_pos_ctrl_estimate
columns.emax_vs_pos_ctrl_ci_upper: Upper bound of the 95% CI for emax_vs_pos_ctrl_estimate

columns.corrected_semi_pure_ec50: EC50 corrected for measured compound concentration (M)
columns.semi_pure_theoretical_mass_on_column: Theoretical mass loaded on the LC column
columns.semi_pure_actual_mass_on_column: Actual mass on column from CAD quantitation
columns.semi_pure_correction_factor: Concentration correction factor applied to potency
columns.semi_pure_cad_peak_area_cv: Coefficient of variation of the CAD peak area
columns.semi_pure_cad_slope_cv: Coefficient of variation of the CAD calibration slope
columns.semi_pure_cad_yield_se: Standard error of the CAD-derived yield

comp_chem/openadmet/pxr/training/single_.description: Single-concentration primary-screen training data (log2 fold-change) — a large, lower-resolution screen useful for pretraining or as auxiliary signal before fine-tuning on the dose-response pEC50 set.

columns.ocnt_batch: Octant batch identifier for the assayed material
columns.log2_fc_estimate: Induction signal as log2 fold-change vs control
columns.t_statistic: t-statistic for the fold-change vs control
columns.cohens_d: Cohen's d effect size for the induction response

comp_chem/pubchem/cyp_inhibition/all_iso.description: Veith CYP inhibition qHTS panel (PubChem AID 1851): ~17k compounds screened in 15-point dose-response against five human CYP isoforms. Unlike the binarized derivatives of this screen (TDC, MoleculeNet), the fitted AC50 is kept as a pIC50 alongside the qHTS curve-quality columns, so it can be used as a regression target. Filter on curve_class and fit_r2 before training. Long format: one row per compound-isoform pair, with the isoform in its own column.

columns.sid: PubChem substance ID for the assayed sample
columns.smiles: Standardized structure (salt-stripped, canonical SMILES) -- use this for modeling and joining
columns.smiles_orig: Structure exactly as deposited with the assay, before standardization
columns.activity_outcome: PubChem call: Active, Inactive, or Inconclusive
columns.isoform: CYP isoform assayed: cyp1a2, cyp2c9, cyp2c19, cyp2d6, or cyp3a4
columns.pic50: -log10(AC50 in M), the negated fit_log_ac50 (prediction target). NaN for inactives, which are left-censored below roughly 4.2 rather than unmeasured
columns.ac50_um: Fitted AC50 in micromolar, as reported by the assay
columns.fit_log_ac50: log10(AC50 in M) from the Hill-equation fit
columns.curve_class: qHTS curve class. -1.1/-1.2 are complete high-quality curves, -2.x partial, -3.0 single-point, 4 inactive (no curve)
columns.fit_r2: R^2 of the Hill-equation fit; closer to 1.0 is a better fit
columns.hill_slope: Hill slope of the fitted dose-response curve
columns.max_response: Maximal response observed across the concentration series

comp_chem/reference_compounds/3d_perf.cs.description: Compounds spanning the size/complexity range used to time the 3D feature endpoints and calibrate their per-instance throughput. Hand-curated reference compounds backing a Workbench regression test; expected values are asserted, so edits here change test outcomes.

comp_chem/reference_compounds/activity_c.description: A single worked activity-cliff example: a pair of near-identical structures with sharply different measured LogD, plus the model's prediction for each. Backs the Dashboard's activity-cliff explainer.

columns.role: Which side of the cliff pair this row is
columns.similarity: Structural similarity to the paired compound
columns.source_model: Workbench model that produced the prediction

comp_chem/reference_compounds/complexity.description: Structures above the 3D complexity budget, which the endpoint must skip rather than attempt. Guards the cost ceiling on conformer generation. Hand-curated reference compounds backing a Workbench regression test; expected values are asserted, so edits here change test outcomes.

columns.name: Compound name
columns.expected_status: Status the 3D endpoint must return (skip reason)

comp_chem/reference_compounds/corner_cas.description: Structures that stress 3D conformer generation -- macrocycles, cages, highly strained systems -- with the status the endpoint must return. Hand-curated reference compounds backing a Workbench regression test; expected values are asserted, so edits here change test outcomes.

columns.name: Compound name
columns.expected_status: Status the 3D endpoint must return for this structure

comp_chem/reference_compounds/flexibilit.description: Compounds spanning the rigid-to-flexible range, used to check that conformer-count tiering scales with rotatable-bond count. Hand-curated reference compounds backing a Workbench regression test; expected values are asserted, so edits here change test outcomes.

comp_chem/reference_compounds/reference_.description: Compounds with expected 3D shape-descriptor ranges (NPR1/NPR2 plane, internal H-bonds, principal axis, nitrogen span) for the smiles-to-3d feature endpoints. Hand-curated reference compounds backing a Workbench regression test; expected values are asserted, so edits here change test outcomes.

columns.name: Compound name
columns.npr1_min: Lower bound on normalized principal moment ratio 1
columns.npr1_max: Upper bound on normalized principal moment ratio 1
columns.npr2_min: Lower bound on normalized principal moment ratio 2
columns.npr2_max: Upper bound on normalized principal moment ratio 2
columns.imhb_min: Lower bound on intramolecular hydrogen bond count
columns.imhb_max: Upper bound on intramolecular hydrogen bond count
columns.axis_min: Lower bound on principal axis length (Angstrom)
columns.axis_max: Upper bound on principal axis length (Angstrom)
columns.nitrogen_span_min: Lower bound on maximum nitrogen-nitrogen distance (Angstrom)
columns.nitrogen_span_max: Upper bound on maximum nitrogen-nitrogen distance (Angstrom)
columns.undefined_chiral_centers_expected: Expected count of undefined chiral centers
columns.stereo_preserved_expected: Whether embedding must preserve the input stereochemistry

comp_chem/reference_compounds/standardiz.description: Input/expected SMILES pairs for the MolStandardizer (salt stripping, charge neutralization, tautomer canonicalization). Hand-curated reference compounds backing a Workbench regression test; expected values are asserted, so edits here change test outcomes.

columns.name: Compound name
columns.expected_smiles: Standardized SMILES the standardizer must produce
columns.expected_salt: Salt/counterion the standardizer must strip, if any
columns.expected_undefined_chiral_centers: Expected count of undefined chiral centers after standardization

comp_chem/reference_compounds/tagging.cs.description: Reference compounds with known expected outputs of workbench.utils.chem_utils.mol_tagging.tag_molecules(). Each row pairs an input SMILES with the standardized SMILES, undefined-chiral count, and the curation-namespace tags that should be emitted after running standardize() then tag_molecules(). Complements the standardization reference set: that set exercises salt / charge / tautomer / stereo handling; this set exercises ADMET-curation tag derivation across composition, structure, physchem, liability, and curation categories. Used as a regression gate — changes that shift any expected tag are either intentional policy updates or bugs.

columns.name: Short identifier for the test case
columns.input_smiles: Raw SMILES fed to standardize() then tag_molecules()
columns.expected_undefined_chiral_centers: Expected value of the 'undefined_chiral_centers' column from standardize() — count of chiral centers in the original input SMILES with no stereo flag
columns.expected_curation_tags: Pipe-delimited list of curation:* tags expected from tag_molecules() (empty string means no curation flags expected)
columns.notes: Why this compound is in the reference set

comp_chem/synthetic/multi_task/log_d.csv.description: Real measured LogD for the 1,000-compound base set -- the genuine task the synthetic LogP recipes are meant to help. One of five files in a controlled multi-task experiment: each synthetic LogP recipe is paired with the same real LogD target, so the only thing varying between runs is how much independent signal the auxiliary task carries.

columns.logd: Auxiliary or target value for this recipe

comp_chem/synthetic/multi_task/log_p.csv.description: Recipe A: pure RDKit Crippen logP. Fully deterministic from structure, so an auxiliary task with no information the model cannot already compute. One of five files in a controlled multi-task experiment: each synthetic LogP recipe is paired with the same real LogD target, so the only thing varying between runs is how much independent signal the auxiliary task carries.

columns.logp: Auxiliary or target value for this recipe

comp_chem/synthetic/multi_task/log_p_ble.description: Recipe B: Crippen logP blended toward measured chemistry, giving an auxiliary task that is partly but not wholly derivable. One of five files in a controlled multi-task experiment: each synthetic LogP recipe is paired with the same real LogD target, so the only thing varying between runs is how much independent signal the auxiliary task carries.

columns.logp: Auxiliary or target value for this recipe

comp_chem/synthetic/multi_task/log_p_rea.description: Recipe D: real measured LogD values on an extended compound set, the strongest and most realistic auxiliary task. One of five files in a controlled multi-task experiment: each synthetic LogP recipe is paired with the same real LogD target, so the only thing varying between runs is how much independent signal the auxiliary task carries.

columns.logp: Auxiliary or target value for this recipe

comp_chem/synthetic/multi_task/log_p_str.description: Recipe C: a random-forest LogD teacher's predictions relabelled as LogP -- an auxiliary task carrying nearly all of the target's signal. One of five files in a controlled multi-task experiment: each synthetic LogP recipe is paired with the same real LogD target, so the only thing varying between runs is how much independent signal the auxiliary task carries.

columns.logp: Auxiliary or target value for this recipe
